narrative.overview: A working tool for one fantasy manager on a laptop. It is the category standard played straight: the density of Basketball Monster, the calm of Linear, the friendliness of Sleeper. Chrome stays neutral and out of the way so the numbers carry the color.
keyCharacteristics: Cool grey ground, white panels, hairline borders.
One indigo accent, used only for actions, the current nav item and selection.
Green/red diverging z-score cells are the main color on screen.
Punting a category greys that column out in every table at once (the signature move).
Light and dark themes follow the OS, from the same tokens.

rules.name: The Numbers Own the Color Rule
rules.body: Chrome is neutral; saturated color appears only where it encodes a number's sign and size, or a primary action.

rules.name: The Dark Mirror Rule
rules.body: Dark mode redefines the same token names under prefers-color-scheme: dark. Components never branch on theme.

rules.name: The No Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No kicker labels above headings. A heading plus a one-line muted description is the whole pattern.

dos: Do show the reason with every verdict: per-category deltas next to the net number.
Do show both sides of a trade (you, them, how it looks to them).
Do use empty states that explain what the panel will show and how to fill it.
Do keep transitions at 120–200ms and only on state changes.
donts: Don't add KPI tile grids or hero metrics.
Don't use the accent for decoration, status or data.
Don't use emoji or Unicode glyphs as icons; draw them in the sprite.
Don't open a modal for anything; everything is inline.
